title: Effect of a lifted action
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x,y$ be finite binary strings, and choose a simulator state, a simulator input-head position $P$, a configuration $c$ of $M$ on input $x$, two work-tape contents $\tau_C,\tau_O$ with head positions $z_C,z_O$, an action $a_w$ on the simulator's three auxiliary tapes, an optional output bit $o$, and an optional successor simulator state $q$. If the first auxiliary tape is left unchanged with no movement, applying the simulator action with no input-head movement produces the simulator configuration with state $q$ and position $P$, the original work tapes and heads of $c$, auxiliary contents given by writing the prescribed values of $a_w$ at $z_C,z_O$, auxiliary head positions $z_C$ and $z_O$ shifted by their prescribed movements, and output consisting of $o$ when present and the empty string otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$a_w$ specifies an action on three auxiliary tapes
$q$ is an optional successor simulator state
$P$ is a simulator input-head position for $y$
The first auxiliary tape action is unchanged and stationary
